name: PT Dharma Satya Nusantara Tbk

frontmatter.title: Dharma Satya Nusantara: a planter priced for a palm-price fall, and an export channel that does not reach it
frontmatter.summary: DSNG sells its whole palm line in Indonesia and exports only wood products and shells, so the single-intermediary export channel reaches it through the domestic parity price and not as a charge. This revision holds the company volume plan, rebuilds non-palm revenue from the segment accounts, widens the levy wedge in the bear and reconciles the DCF multiple. BUY at Rp2,800, a 115.2% total return from Rp1,325.
thesis: The DCF enterprise value of IDR33.85tn is a first-forecast-year multiple: on next year's EBITDA it is within a tenth of a turn of the 6.3x the cross-check applies, so the two legs are one view of the cycle, not two [S3, S4].
At Rp1,325 the market discounts a palm price of US$1,040/t, below spot and well below the deck, so the disagreement is about the recovery and not about today [S0, S8].
Volume follows the company's own projection of 1.0% growth rather than a trimmed number: no source cuts the plan, so the base case does not [S4, F60].
The levy-plus-freight wedge, not a proportional haircut, sets the realised price: a wider wedge takes the value to about nine tenths of the target and the return to five sixths of the base [S6, F36].

The index decision is a de-rating the palm price cannot offset: a one-point cost-of-equity premium takes the value to about nineteen twentieths of the target, and it is the first signpost we watch [S11].

catalysts.event: Revision to PP 24/2026 implementing the DSI single-intermediary channel, expected in mid-November; the tariff and price-range rules are still unfinalised
Monthly export duty and levy reset and the December reference price
DSI channel takes effect for coal, CPO and ferroalloy exports
Annual general meeting and dividend approval for the year to December

blocks.text: The news is confirmed: from 1 January 2027 coal, crude palm oil and ferroalloy exports pass through PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI) as sole intermediary, which will set a fair export price range referenced to the HPE through a rulebook still to be written [S12, S13, S15]. For DSNG the direct reach is nil: the palm segment sold its entire nine-month line of IDR8,059.2bn domestically with nil export sales, and the export line is IDR977.3bn of wood products and palm-kernel shells, neither named in the announcement [S2, F61, F72, F75, F76]. The channel that matters is the domestic parity price — the reference price less the export duty and levy — and it is unquantified because no tariff and no range formula has been published [S6, S15, F36].

This revision holds the company's own volume plan instead of a trimmed number, rebuilds non-palm revenue from the segment accounts, carries the wider levy wedge in the bear, sizes the standalone-index de-rating and reconciles the DCF's multiple with the cross-check. The result is BUY at a twelve-month value of Rp2,800, a total return of 115.2% from Rp1,325, of which 111.3% is price appreciation and the balance the next-twelve-month dividend. The DSI channel decides who files and at what price range; the DHE SDA relaxation governs how much foreign currency an exporter may convert; neither changes volume, cost or the deck today [S9, S10, S12].

DSNG is an integrated oil-palm producer: 111,900 ha planted hectares, split between nucleus estates it owns and plasma blocks it develops for smallholders, with mills in East, Central and West Kalimantan; a wood-products business making engineered flooring and panels in Central Java; and a renewables business exporting palm-kernel shells and wood pellets to Japan and Korea [S4, S7, F38]. Last year CPO production reached 631 kt, sales 629 kt and the extraction rate 23.3% [S3, F1, F23, F26].

Almost all of the value is palm: the segment took 88.0% of nine-month revenue of 9,110 IDR bn, and the export line is almost entirely the other two segments [S2, F54, F31]. Strategy is unglamorous: replant older blocks, finish the plasma programme, delever, add small downstream projects such as a bio-CNG plant using mill effluent [S4, S7]. There is no large acquisition, so the capital question is whether dividend and replanting can both be funded from operating cash flow, and last year they were [S3, F50]. The company is controlled by the Triputra and Oetomo families, holding 30.6% and 29.2%, with an Oetomo family member as president director [S4, F55, F56]. It holds the estate through operating subsidiaries and a stake in an associated estate in East Kalimantan, with a small non-controlling interest, no dual-class structure and no share pledge; the bank debt is secured on bearer plants of IDR2,605.8bn, inventories of IDR227.6bn and receivables of IDR135.5bn [S2, F82, F83, F84].

The palm price is the largest driver. The house deck runs CPO from US$886/t in 2023 to US$1,007/t last year, US$1,135/t this year and US$1,240/t next, then fades to US$1,150/t long-run [S0]. The series is the World Bank Pink Sheet, whose annual averages for the three audited years are US$886/t in 2023, US$963/t in 2024 and US$1,007/t in 2025 [S16]. The deck's long-run marker sits above every print of those three years, so the terminal value is a premium to the observed average, not a haircut to spot [S16, S0]. Supply is tight: GAPKI expects Indonesian output to fall by 2,200 kt in 2027 as the long dry spell lands, and says that is the complete El Nino impact [S8, F37]. DSNG's own experience is consistent: nine-month fruit output 1,500 kt, CPO 451 kt [S5, F35, F34].

Policy is set monthly. The Ministry of Trade sets a reference price and derives the export duty and levy from it; for November the reference price is US$979/t and the combined charge US$246/t, down a fifth on October's US$308/t [S6, F36, F48, F77]. Because the charge is a dollar amount per tonne, not a proportional cut, the wedge shrinks as a ratio when the benchmark rises, which is what our realisation assumption carries [S6, S3]. The biodiesel mandate is the other pillar: the government confirmed the B50 blend, and palm use for biodiesel was 1,350 kt in August while exports rose and stocks fell [S6, F49]. No published formula sets the domestic price; it is negotiated against export parity, so a DSI charge or a binding range reaches a domestic seller through the same parity [S6, S12, S13]. GAPKI has asked that DSI stay an intermediary, warning that an unclear scheme adds cost [S14].

Competitive position is cost and certification, not share. DSNG is a small producer and a price taker, but its cash cost per tonne is set by its own estate and mill efficiency, with mills close to the fruit and an extraction rate above the industry average [S4, F26]. It has no pricing power, which is why it is valued on a through-cycle price rather than a multiple of one year's earnings [S3]. The market backdrop is a separate risk: MSCI is consulting on reclassifying Indonesia to standalone and the country's emerging-market weight has shrunk to a fraction of one per cent, so few global holders have an interest in opposing it [S11]. For a domestic mid-cap with a 33.1% free float that is a de-rating with nothing to do with palm oil [S11, S0].

The last audited year is the anchor. Revenue was 12,315 IDR bn, cost of revenue 8,465 IDR bn and gross profit IDR3,850.0bn [S3, F5, F7]. Cost of revenue carries D&A of 974 IDR bn, which the data pack understated by an order of magnitude, so depreciation is restated to the audited note; on that basis EBITDA was IDR3,814.6bn at a margin of 31.0% [S3, F9].

Every EBITDA here is operating EBITDA: audited operating profit plus depreciation of fixed assets and right-of-use assets plus amortisation of bearer plants and intangibles, with the associate excluded and with no add-back of the impairment or deduction of the biological gain [S3]. It sits a fraction of a per cent above operating profit of IDR2,829.4bn plus D&A of IDR973.7bn. The audited reconciliation prints IDR4,078.0bn: the difference is the associate's IDR168.4bn plus the IDR116.9bn impairment less the IDR10.4bn biological gain, which we strip because the associate's earnings cannot sit inside the multiple while its book value sits in the bridge [S3, F52, F64-F67, F44].

After deducting the cost of non-palm revenue at a normal margin, the cash cost of a tonne of CPO is about IDR8.0m, or USD456 a tonne [S3, F7, F9]. That is well below the US$886.0 trough of the last three audited years and a fraction of the November reference price of US$979/t, so the estate is cash-positive at any observed price; we cannot source a global cost curve that carries DSNG, so we state the comparison rather than claim a numbered quartile [S16, F79, F48]. The mature plantation is amortised over a productive life of 20, and 111,900 ha planted hectares over that life is about four and a half thousand hectares of replanting a year, so last year's capex of 856 IDR bn at eighty-eight per cent of D&A is replacement, not a haircut [S3, F85, F38, F9, F11]. Costs are held at the last actual in real terms, inflated at the long-run rupiah anchor, which is also the terminal growth rate [S0, S3]. The plasma outlay is excluded because collections in the same investing section reimburse it [S3, F11].

Volume is the company's own plan. We carry 637.0 thousand tonnes, the printed 1.0% growth applied to the 631 kt produced last year, with a realised price of US$859.2 a tonne, revenue of IDR12,781.6bn, EBITDA of IDR4,095.3bn and earnings per share of Rp191.4 [S4, F60, F23, S3]. The nine-month outturn of 451 kt is below the prior year, so the plan needs a strong fourth quarter; that risk sits in the bear volume leg [S5, F34]. The realisation ratio of 0.76 comes from the segment accounts and the deck's exchange rate [S2, F31, F34, S4].

Next year the deck does the work. The ratio is not held flat: the accounts show a dollar wedge between benchmark and realised price that behaves like a levy-plus-freight amount, so we hold the wedge and let the ratio rise with the benchmark, and beyond the explicit years hold it at its final level [S2, S6, F36, F48]. Revenue reaches IDR14,448.6bn and EBITDA IDR5,434.7bn [S0, S3]. Volume is flat because the source the deck rests on says next year is the El Nino trough [S8, F37, S5].

The nine months put the cycle on the same operating basis. Revenue was 9,110 IDR bn and the printed EBITDA of 2,950 IDR bn was up about a per cent [S2, F31, F33]. On our definition the nine months are operating profit of IDR2,113.5bn plus D&A of IDR733.2bn; the printed line is higher by the associate's IDR144.4bn and lower by the IDR41.4bn biological gain [S2, F68-F71]. Profit attributable to owners was IDR1,465.0bn against total profit of IDR1,441.7bn, the difference the negative non-controlling interest [S2, F32, F78]. Operating cash flow of 1,912 IDR bn fell as the prior year's working-capital release reversed, and the company paid the 498 IDR bn dividend [S2, F41, F42].

The non-palm line is built, not escalated. Last year's non-CPO revenue of IDR3,216.9bn is palm kernel and kernel oil, wood and renewables [S3, F29]. Kernel is a palm by-product and scales with CPO volume; wood and renewables are held at the nine-month run-rate annualised, below last year because wood revenue fell and its margin with it [S2]. No wood recovery is assumed, so a DHE-driven recovery is upside [S9, S10]. The blended gross margin of 20.0% is a blend: kernel earns the palm-segment margin, wood a fifth of it last year and less in the nine months [S3, S2].

The balance sheet is in good shape: forecast net debt at the year end of IDR1,903.3bn is under half of this year's EBITDA, against attributable equity of 11,481 IDR bn [S2, S3, F15]. The dividend at a payout of 27.1% and the replanting inside own capex are the claims on cash [S3, F21]. Earnings quality: accruals are negative in both fiscal years and in the nine months, and operating cash flow has exceeded net profit in every period [S3, S2, F13, F50, F41]. Purchases from the Daiken associate are 0.7% of raw-material purchases and the payable to it 0.3% of trade payables, with no sales to related parties disclosed [S2, F58, F59]. On the IDX regime test we can source the 2013 listing [S4] but not the exchange's board or notation status — the fetcher refuses idx.co.id by design — so we assert none; the one optics-class item is the land revaluation surplus of 2,585 IDR bn, which inflates book equity but not cash flow [S3, F57].

We value DSNG on a DCF as the primary method, with an EV/EBITDA and a P/BV cross-check. The DCF carries the controlling weight because the company is a price-taking commodity producer whose value is a long stream of cash flows at a through-cycle price, while a multiple capitalises whatever point of the cycle its year sits on [S3, S4]. The new export policy changes none of the cash flows: no fee and no binding range exists to put into them, and the palm sales remain domestic [S12, S13, S15, F61].

The cost of capital comes from the house macro deck and the industry configuration: a rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4% less the default spread of 1.6%, plus a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, on an unlevered beta of 0.80 that relevers to 0.94 [S2]. That gives a cost of equity of 12.1% and a WACC of 11.3% at a debt weight of 18.8%; the cost of debt of 9.4% is the marginal rate [S3]. Terminal growth of 2.5% is the long-run rupiah inflation [S0].
The DCF produces Rp3,077 per share, with the terminal value at 45.7% of enterprise value, and free cash flow rising from IDR2,334.7bn this year to IDR2,907.9bn in five years [S0, S3].

The DCF enterprise value is IDR33,848bn; against this year's operating EBITDA of IDR4,095bn that is well above the 6.3x the cross-check applies and the 3.9x the market pays [S3, S4]. The gap is the first forecast year: against next year's EBITDA of IDR5,435bn the same enterprise value is just below the 6.3x of the cross-check. The DCF is therefore not paying a premium multiple through the cycle: it capitalises a rising stream at the multiple the cross-check already endorses [S3, S4]. The market's 3.9x is the outlier.

The two cross-checks sit below: EV/EBITDA applies 6.3x to last year's operating EBITDA of 3,814.6 — the definition section three sets out, not the audited reconciliation line of IDR4,078.0bn — for Rp2,165, -29.7% against the primary [S3, F64]. P/BV applies 1.3x to pre-revaluation book equity of IDR9,862.6bn, attributable equity less the land surplus of IDR2,585.1bn, for Rp1,181, -61.6% against the primary [S2, F62, F63]. Pre-revaluation book is what the earnings-quality card requires, because the surplus never reaches cash flow and would flatter the multiple by roughly a quarter; a book multiple also cannot see the cash between replantings, so the leg is a floor [S3, F57, S4].

The associate is in the bridge at book: IDR1,578.9bn, about nine times last year's share of its profit of IDR168.4bn and above the group's own 7.6x, so book is not an obviously cheap mark; on the annualised nine-month share — a third again the IDR144.4bn booked in the nine months — it is a little under eight times [S2, F44, F52, F70]. One extra turn on that annualised profit would add about half a per cent of the IDR33,848bn enterprise value, so we keep book.

The reverse DCF is the cleanest statement of the mispricing. At Rp1,325 the market discounts a palm price of US$1,040/t on our cost base and cost of capital, which is 83.9% of the deck's next-year level [S0, S3]. Set against spot of US$1,180/t and this year's deck of US$1,135/t, the market is not assuming the price stays where it is: it assumes a fall, and then no recovery [S8, F37]. That is the disagreement: we need the GAPKI decline and the deck's recovery, the market needs the price to keep falling [S8]. If the deck is right the shares are worth materially more; if the market is right the bear is the relevant value [S3, S6].

The sensitivity table shows what matters. A palm-price move passes almost straight to the margin, a volume move carries a cost because the estate's costs are largely fixed, and the exchange rate acts like a price move because revenue is dollar-denominated and cost is rupiah [S0, S3]. The grid's centre sits below the published base because the grid holds the long-run price at the shocked level while the base escalates it with rupiah inflation; read it for relative sensitivity [S0, S3]. The four-fifths column is the through-cycle case for a sceptic, and it is close to the market's implied price [S0, S16].

The bear cuts the palm price a fifth, trims volume a twentieth, strengthens the rupiah a tenth and widens the levy-plus-freight wedge a tenth, and values the shares at Rp806, below the current price [S3, S6]. The wedge rather than a proportional realisation hit is the risk at this exposure: a progressive levy, or a DSI fair-price range that lifts the declared export value and with it the reference price and levy base, widens it by more [S6, F36, F77, S15]. The base case is Rp2,825 and the bull Rp4,746, at 25%, 50% and 25% [S3]. The bull moves the same four drivers the other way, so the spread is the operating leverage of the estate [S3, S8].

We sized the two risks a commodity scenario cannot carry. A levy fifty dollars a tonne wider than the November charge takes the value to about nine tenths of Rp2,800 and the return from 115.2% to about five sixths of the base; it is the largest single policy number in the file, and why the wedge rather than the benchmark is the variable to watch [S6, F36, F48]. The standalone-index de-rating is a cost of equity event: a one-point premium takes the value to about nineteen twentieths of Rp2,800 and the return to about nine tenths, and it does not reverse if the palm price rises [S11, S0]. Neither sits in the three cases: the first is inside the bear's wedge leg, and the second is one-sided because Indonesia is already in the index [S11].

The operating risks are ordinary. A sustained fall in the dollar price hits revenue directly and widens the domestic discount if the levy is not cut in step [S6, S8]. El Nino has already cut fruit production, and a second dry year would push the recovery out and raise unit cost as fixed costs spread over fewer tonnes [S5, F35]. Policy reaches the domestic price without changing the company's cost [S6, S15, S13]. At Rp18,140/USD the rupiah is close to its weakest on record, which helps revenue and raises the rupiah cost of imported inputs [S6, F47]. Replanting reduces the mature area before it increases it, and a delay in plasma slows the volume recovery [S4].

Liquidity is adequate but not deep: average daily traded value of IDR7.5bn, a free float of 33.1% and a twelve-month range of Rp1,075.0 to Rp1,860.0 [S0]. A large holder would need patience, the same channel through which the index decision acts [S0]. The signposts are specific: an MSCI decision, or a timetable that makes reclassification likely [S11]; a published DSI tariff or range above current invoices, a levy increase, or a second quarter of falling fruit production [S15, S6, S5]; on the other side a confirmed GAPKI decline with a rising reference price [S8, F48].

DSNG is controlled by two families: the Triputra interests hold 30.6% and the Oetomo interests 29.2%, with a further block held by an investment company [S4, S3, F55, F56]. The ultimate beneficiaries named in the annual report are Ny. T.P. Rachmat L.R. Imanto and Andrianto Oetomo, and the president director is an Oetomo family member, so control and management are the same people [S4]. The public holds 33.1%, comfortably above the minimum [S0, S4].

The audit is clean: Siddharta Widjaja and Rekan, the Indonesian member firm of KPMG, unmodified in all material respects, with independent commissioners alongside executive directors, no dual-class structure and no share pledge — the security is over bearer plants, inventory and receivables [S4, S3, S2, F82]. Related-party dealings are modest: trade payables to related parties were 2.0 IDR bn at the end of September against third-party payables many times larger, and the associated estate is a related party because the company holds a stake in it [S2, S3, F53, F44]. A loan to that associate was repaid in full in April 2025, so there is no related-party financing exposure [S3, F52].

The dividend record is consistent: Rp47.0/share declared for the last financial year and Rp24.0/share the year before, a payout of about 27.1% of earnings [S3, F21, F22]. It is covered by free cash flow and sits inside the stated policy band [S3, F50, F11]. At through-cycle free cash flow the equity generates an FCFE yield of 15.0% against a dividend yield of 3.9%, so the net cash build to -2,695.9 by FY2028 is reachable as a higher payout rather than stranded [S3, F21, S4].

On ESG the certification stack is the strongest part: every mill is ISPO certified, most are RSPO certified, and the nucleus estates are certified at a high share under both [S4]. The company took impact investment financing from the &Green fund and runs a bio-CNG plant that captures mill effluent, and the plasma programme gives smallholders a stake and reduces land-conflict risk [S4, F38]. The remaining exposures are industry-standard: European deforestation rules, weak flooring demand, and land and labour risk across 19,037 employees [S4, S7, S0].

The nearest catalyst is the DSI rulebook: the changes go into a revision of PP 24/2026 expected in mid-November, with the tariff and price range to be published before the 1 January 2027 start [S15, S13]. When the tariff appears the arithmetic is direct — a charge of one per cent of export value on next year's benchmark is about twelve dollars a tonne, a little over one per cent of the reference price, and it widens the wedge the way the November levy did [S15, F36, F48]. We will size it against the realisation assumption. The secondary question is scope: whether shells and pellets, which the renewables segment ships to Japan and Korea, are drawn in [S12, F76].

The second is the monthly policy reset: the November package cut the charge to US$246/t while the reference price fell to US$979/t, so parity was flat, and the December print is what matters for the fourth quarter [S6, F36, F48]. The third is the fourth-quarter production report, which shows whether the El Nino decline in Kalimantan has turned [S5, F35]. The fourth is the full-year result and the dividend: on our forecast the dividend per share rises to Rp52 over the next twelve months, a yield of 3.9% [S3, F21]. The fifth is the GAPKI data flow, testing the 2,200 kt 2027 decline month by month [S8, F37].

Between updates we monitor six things: the MSCI consultation, the DSI tariff and price-range rules, the monthly reference price and levy, quarterly fruit and CPO volumes, the realised price per tonne implied by segment revenue, and unit cash cost and net debt [S11, S15, S6, S5, S2, S3].

valuation.label: EV/EBITDA
valuation.basis: average of peer median and own five-year average

valuation.label: P/BV
valuation.basis: average of peer median and own five-year average

bear.narrative: El Nino persists into 2027, the CPO deck gives back a fifth of its level and DSNG volumes miss the plan by 5%; the rupiah strengthens a tenth; and the levy-plus-freight wedge widens a tenth — a progressive levy or a DSI fair-price range that lifts the reference-price and levy base, about double the November levy swing — so the rupiah price falls twice over and the dividend with it. The MSCI standalone risk is a de-rating, not an earnings shock, so it is sized separately and listed as the first signpost rather than stacked here.

bull.narrative: A stronger 2027 supply deficit after the GAPKI 2.2m-tonne decline lifts CPO a fifth above the deck, El Nino recovery plus plasma maturities add 5% to volume, the rupiah weakens a tenth and a levy cut that is not matched by a lower reference price widens net export parity by a tenth — the November move carried through — so the rupiah price compounds. The four drivers are the same four the bear moves, in the opposite direction, so the spread in the values is the operating leverage of the estate, not a different set of assumptions.

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

assumptions.label: CPO sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 637 kt is the company's own plan: the projection is printed as a growth rate of 1% on the FY2025 realisation [F60, S4 p.129], applied to the 631,046 t base [F23]. The method holds the base case to the plan unless a source says otherwise, and no source cuts it. The 651 kt printed in the same row is the FY2025 TARGET, which the 631 kt realisation missed [F46, F23]; it is not a current-year work plan. The nine-month outturn of 451 kt [F34] is 1.5% down, so hitting the plan needs a Q4 above last year's, which is what the company's own projection assumes; the risk that it misses sits in the bear volume leg, not in an unsourced trim here. FY2027E is held at the plan level because GAPKI says the 2.2m-tonne Indonesian decline in 2027 is the full El Nino effect [F37, S8] while DSNG's own nine-month FFB is down 4.3% with Q3 down 5.7% q/q [F35, S5]; the recovery starts in FY2028E as the affected blocks and the 29,000 ha of plasma estates mature, adding about 30 kt by FY2030E against planted area of 111,900 ha [F38], the same recovery increment as before, rebased on the plan.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is derived from the segment accounts alone, not fitted to an EBITDA line: nine-month 2026 palm-segment revenue of 8,059.213 [S2] on 451 kt of CPO production [F34] is Rp17.87m per tonne; CPO sales track production (FY2025 sales 628.737 kt against production 631.046 kt, 99.6% [F1, F23]), so the production denominator is immaterial. Stripping by-products at the FY2025 per-tonne value (1,748.322 of non-CPO palm revenue on 628.737 kt = Rp2.781m [F5, F29]) leaves Rp15.09m per tonne of CPO, or USD 859/t at the deck's FY2026E rupiah of 17,570 [S4], which is 0.757 of the deck's USD 1,135/t benchmark. At the FY2025 actual rate of 16,448 the same rupiah price is USD 917/t, 0.808 of the benchmark: the bracket is the exchange-rate choice, and we use the deck's forward rate because the forecast year's revenue is translated at it. The model's FY2026E operating EBITDA is an output of that ratio, not an input to it; it lands near the nine-month operating line because both come from the same accounts, and that coincidence is a check rather than independent evidence. From FY2027E the ratio is derived from the dollar wedge instead of being held flat: the November reference price of 978.90 less the 246.36 levy gives net export parity of 732.5 against 733.9 in October [F48, F36], and the wedge of about 276-281 USD/t is a levy-plus-freight amount, not a proportional haircut, so the ratio rises as the benchmark rises. Beyond the explicit years the ratio is held at its final explicit-year level (lt 0.761), because the levy and the freight reset with the reference price and with dollar costs, so the wedge escalates with the benchmark in the terminal years. The DSI single-intermediary export channel from 1 January 2027 is a wedge risk but not a modelled input: DSNG exports no CPO [F61], so any DSI fee or imposed export price range reaches it only through the domestic price its refinery buyers pay, and DSI has not published either a tariff or a range formula [S12, S13, S15].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No domestic price cap applies to CPO; the DMO obligation is on producers' export allocation, not on the price received.

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (bcm per tonne equivalent)
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 so that cost_per_bcm is read directly as rupiah of cash cost per tonne of CPO sold; DSNG is an estate, not a mine, and there is no overburden to strip.

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (IDR)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 cash COGS = cost of revenue 8,464.728 less D&A 973.744 = 7,490.984 [F7, F9]; less the cost of the 3,216.888 of non-CPO revenue at a 20% gross margin = 2,573.510, leaving 4,917.474 for 628.737 kt = Rp7.821m per tonne [F1, F29]. Escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation in the macro deck.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of cash cost
assumptions.basis: No separate fuel index is modelled: diesel is inside the rupiah cash cost per tonne, which already carries the FY2025 actual fuel bill.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero: haulage, milling and overhead are already inside the audited cost of revenue from which cost_per_bcm is derived, so adding a second per-tonne charge would double-count.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: No royalty: Indonesian oil-palm estates pay the export levy only on exports, and the geographic segment note shows the entire palm-oil line, 8,059.213 in the nine months, sold into the local market with nil export sales [F61, S2]. The levy therefore reaches DSNG through the domestic price, not as a charge on its own sales [F36].

assumptions.label: Other revenue (PK, PKO, wood products, renewables)
assumptions.basis: Built in two parts, not held flat by default. FY2025 non-CPO revenue 3,216.888 = PK/PKO 1,748.322 + wood 1,242.325 + renewables 226.241 [F5, F29, S3]. The PK/PKO line is a palm by-product and scales with CPO volume, so FY2026E carries it at the plan volume: 1,748.322 x 637/631 = 1,764.6. Wood and renewables are held at the nine-month run-rate annualised, 1,050.596 x 4/3 = 1,400.8, which is below the FY2025 level of 1,468.566 because wood revenue fell to 897.400 in the nine months and its gross margin to 5.5% while renewables held at 23.0% [S2]; that is the segment accounts, not a default haircut, and no wood or flooring recovery is assumed in the base, so a DHE-driven or flooring recovery is upside. FY2026E total 3,165.4, escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation thereafter.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: 20% is the blend across the whole non-CPO line, not the wood-and-renewables margin. FY2025: palm segment revenue 10,846.146 and gross profit 3,660.509, wood 1,242.325 and 138.887 (11.2%), renewables 226.241 and 50.588 (22.4%) [S3]. The non-CPO line is PK/PKO 1,748.322 plus wood and renewables 1,468.566; at the palm-segment margin on PK/PKO and the reported margins on the other two, the blend is 20.0% and reconciles the group gross profit of 3,849.984 [S3]. Nine-month 2026: palm 8,059.213 and 2,826.156 (35.1%), wood 897.400 and 49.676 (5.5%), renewables 153.196 and 35.212 (23.0%) [S2]; the wood margin halved but the palm margin rose, so the same blend still holds. The red team's 8.1% is the wood-plus-renewables subset only, 1,050.596 of 9,109.809 revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A per tonne (IDR)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total D&A 973.744 [F9] over 628.737 kt of CPO sold [F1] = Rp1.549m per tonne; escalated at 2.5% rupiah inflation. The pack's Rp65.922bn D&A line is not a D&A figure and is restated to the audited note.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per tonne (IDR)
assumptions.basis: The 88%-of-D&A ratio is the company's own replacement programme, not a haircut, and the replanting plan supports it line by line. FY2025 own capex 856.267 = fixed-asset additions 648.177 + capitalised plantation cost 208.090 [F11] over 628.737 kt [F1] = Rp1.362m per tonne. Split against the D&A components [F9]: fixed-asset additions 648.177 against fixed-asset depreciation 692.004 is 94%, and capitalised plantation 208.090 against bearer-plant and intangible amortisation of about 265.4 is 78% — but replanting is booked at current cost while the amortisation runs on historical cost, so a rupiah of replanting replaces more than a rupiah of the amortisation charge. On the physical cycle 111,900 planted hectares [F38] over roughly 25 years is about 4,500 hectares a year, and 208.090 of capitalised plantation is the full programme at that rate; there is no under-replacement, and the two lines are not the same asset base. Held at the last actual in real terms and escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation (macro deck inflation_idr_lt, the BI target midpoint [S4]). The plasma outlay of 943.660 is excluded because the 1,019.857 of plasma collections in the same investing section reimburses it [F11].

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero: no separately disclosed expansion project is funded in the plan; the company's 2026 budget is maintenance and replanting, which sits in capex_unit.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital 1,144.975 / revenue 12,314.712 = 9.3%; the three-year average of 11.5% is inflated by the FY2022 inventory build, so the last actual is used.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax 670.747 / pre-tax profit 2,499.545 = 26.8%, held flat; the group has no material deferred-tax asset to run down.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs 452.485 [F18] / opening debt 5,733.094 = 7.9%; the 2020 sustainability bond of 181.924 was repaid during FY2025 (bonds payable nil at 31-Dec-2025, 181.924 at 31-Dec-2024, and 181.924 repaid in the FY2025 cash flow) [S3], and the remaining bank debt reprices off JIBOR, so the rate is held.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income 12.552 [F19] / opening cash 557.023 = 2.25%; most operating cash sits in current accounts rather than time deposits.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: debt fell from 5,733.094 to 4,105.200 in FY2025 and to 3,247.177 by 30-Sep-2026 [S2], and the stated policy is deleveraging, so no new net debt is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: no recurring non-operating line; the FY2025 gap between reported pre-tax profit and EBIT less net interest is the capitalised-interest adjustment, which is not a run-rate item.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the non-controlling interest is Rp139.699bn of equity and its share of profit was negative in FY2025, so it is immaterial to the parent valuation.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS of Rp47 [F21] on EPS of Rp173.63 (profit 1,840.490 [F13] over 10,599.8424m shares [F20]) = 27.1%, inside the stated 25-30% policy band.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 10,599,842,400 shares issued and outstanding with no buyback or option overhang disclosed [F20].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.5%: the long-run rupiah inflation in the macro deck, consistent with a terminal CPO price that is flat in real terms and a mature estate that cannot outgrow the planting base.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A and other opex 1,009.092 / revenue 12,314.712 = 8.19%; the three-year average of 8.96% is lifted by the FY2022-23 cost base, so the last actual is used.

challenges.challenge: s3 says Daiken purchases are 68.0 pct of raw-material purchases and the payable 30.0 pct of all trade payables [S2, F58, F59], but note 38 says 0,68 pct and 0,30 pct (S2 p.92), so both are overstated 100x and contradict s6's description of third-party payables as many times larger.
challenges.answer: F58 and F59 already held 0.68 and 0.30 with unit percent; the report applied a pct formatter that multiplied by 100, so it now prints fact.F58 and fact.F59 with no formatter and reads 0.68% and 0.30%, consistent with note 38 and with section 6 describing third-party payables as many times larger [S2].

challenges.challenge: s3 says profit attributable to owners was 1,442 citing F32, but 1,441.702 is total profit; the owners' share is 1,465.045 (EPS 138.21 on 10,599.8m shares) with negative NCI of 23.343, so F32 is mislabelled np_parent.
challenges.answer: F32 was the consolidated TOTAL profit of 1,441.702 and is relabelled and rekeyed np_9m; new F78 carries the attributable line 1,465.045 after negative NCI of 23.343, which is the line that agrees with EPS of 138.21 on 10,599.84m shares. Section 3 now states both [S2].

challenges.challenge: The reverse-DCF implied CPO is USD1,044 in s4 (model factor 0.842 x 1,240) but USD1,068 and 14 pct below deck in the extreme_call QC justification; the current run gives 1,044, which is 16 pct below.
challenges.answer: Reconciled to the current run: factor 0.839 on the FY2027E deck of 1,240 gives an implied CPO of USD1,040, which is 16% below the deck and is now the only number quoted; the stale 1,068 and 14% in the extreme_call justification are removed [S0, S4].

challenges.challenge: s4 says the market is assuming the price stays roughly where it is now, but its own reverse DCF of USD1,044 is about 12 pct below spot of USD1,180 and below the FY2026 deck of 1,135, so the market is pricing a fall, not flatness.
challenges.answer: Restated: market-implied CPO of USD1,040 is 12% below spot of 1,180 and 8% below the FY2026E deck of 1,135, so the market is pricing a fall and then no recovery, not flatness. Section 4 now argues the mispricing on that basis, naming the GAPKI 2.2m-tonne decline as what we need to be right [S0, S8].

challenges.challenge: The DCF carries 60 pct weight and implies 8.3x FY2026E and 8.6x FY2025A EBITDA (EV 32,957 / 3,982 and 3,815), against the analyst's own 6.34x multiple and the market's 4.05x; s4 explains only the P/BV gap of -61 pct, leaving the EV/EBITDA gap of -28 pct unreconciled.
challenges.answer: The 8.3x is a first-forecast-year artifact, not a cycle premium: DCF EV 33,838 on FY2026E EBITDA 4,095 is 8.3x, on FY2027E EBITDA 5,435 it is 6.2x, on FY2030E 6.8x, and the terminal of 40,991 on FY2035 EBITDA of 5,948 is an implied exit of 6.9x, so the DCF capitalises at the same 6.34x the cross-check applies. Section 4 now runs the three multiples side by side; weights stay 60/25/15 because the two legs no longer disagree [S3, S4].

challenges.challenge: The through-cycle CPO anchor (deck fades to about USD1,150 long-run, FY2027 1,240) is not tied to a named 10y real average or cost-curve incentive price as VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL step 2 requires; the DCF rests on the house deck alone and the deck's long-run source is not shown.
challenges.answer: Through-cycle marker now sourced: the World Bank Pink Sheet October 2026 (S16) puts the CPO annual average at 886, 963 and 1,007 USD/t for 2023-2025; the deck long-run of 1,150 sits above all three and section 2 says so, with the price grid at four-fifths of the deck as the through-cycle NAV [S16, S0].

challenges.challenge: The base holds the levy-plus-freight wedge at about USD281/t flat through 2030 (FY2026 realisation 0.757 versus FY2025 0.874) and the bear carries only a -7 pct realisation shock; a progressive levy or a DSI fair-price range that lifts the reference price and levy base is not scenarioed at 88 pct palm exposure.
challenges.answer: Bear realisation widened from 0.93 to 0.90 with the levy-wedge narrative, and the wedge is sized separately: a levy plus USD50/t (ratio 0.948) takes the twelve-month value to 2,568 and the total return to 97.1% from 115.2%, a 8.3% cut, cited to the November levy move [S6, F36, F77].

challenges.challenge: s2 says section five tests the MSCI standalone de-rating rather than assuming the discount is only commodity, but s5 applies a 0.0 pct liquidity discount and calls liquidity not a valuation input; no COE or WACC sensitivity exists in the model, whose grids vary only price, FX, volume and cost.
challenges.answer: Sized with the engine: a one-percentage-point cost-of-equity premium for a standalone Indonesia takes the twelve-month value to 2,659 and the total return to 104.6%, a 5.0% cut, and it does not reverse with a higher palm price. It is stated in section 5 and as the first signpost, not stacked into the bear because the house limit is four shocks and Indonesia is already in the index so the risk is one-sided [S11].

challenges.challenge: The 35 pct PT REA Kaltim associate is added to the bridge at book Rp1,579bn and no house or market value is attempted; its 9M 2026 income of 144.4bn implies roughly 8x at book, so any higher EBITDA would understate the add.
challenges.answer: Book is the most likely mark, shown: the 1,578.868 stake is 9.4x last year associate income of 168.385 and 8.2x the annualised nine-month 144.430, against the group own P/E of 7.6x, so it is not understated; each extra turn adds about Rp18 a share, a little over one per cent of EV, and section 4 states that sensitivity [S2, S3, F44, F52, F70].

challenges.challenge: Wood and renewables (26 pct of revenue) are carried at a blended 20 pct gross margin with no separate valuation; wood ran at 11.2 pct in FY2025 and is the cyclical export leg the DHE relaxation and a flooring recovery would help, so the recovery is not valued.
challenges.answer: Segment accounts are now in the section 3 non-palm paragraph: kernel earns the palm margin, wood earned 11.2% last year and 5.5% in the nine months, renewables 22.4% and 23.0%, so the 20% blend is not a wood recovery; no wood or flooring recovery is valued, and it is labelled as upside [S3, S2].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E volume of 615 kt is 3.5 pct below the company's own +1 pct plan (~637 kt, S4 p.129) and below the Q4-seasonal run-rate (~624 kt); the basis concedes the plan but does not source the shortfall, a downward drift on the largest revenue driver.
challenges.answer: Volume now follows the plan: 637 kt in FY2026E, the printed 1% growth on the 631,046 t realisation, held at 637 kt in FY2027E and rising to 667 kt by FY2030E on the same recovery increment; no source cut the plan, so the base no longer does, and EBITDA and the DCF are rebuilt on it [S4, F60, F23].

challenges.challenge: other_revenue of 3,297bn (26 pct of revenue) is escalated at 2.5 pct with no volume growth assumed for the wood and renewable segments and no source, a default zero-growth haircut on the second-largest revenue line.
challenges.answer: Other revenue is now built, not escalated flat: kernel and kernel oil are carried at the plan CPO volume and wood plus renewables at the nine-month run-rate annualised, which is 4.6% below FY2025 because wood revenue and margin fell. FY2026E revenue is Rp132bn lower and EBITDA about Rp26bn lower, under one per cent of the DCF leg; wood recovery is upside [S2, S3, S9, S10].

challenges.challenge: The report is 7,194 words against a 3,500 guide and has grown from 5,633 in the prior round; the roughly 1,300-word DSI addition concludes no model change yet repeats the same verdict in the summary, s2, s3 and s7.
challenges.answer: Cut from 7,194 to 4,396 words: the DSI material is now two paragraphs in the summary and one in section 2, the repetition across sections 2, 3 and 7 is gone, and the sensitivity and monitoring paragraphs are single. Still above the 3,500 guide; further cuts would remove evidence the same review demanded, so it is flagged rather than padded.

challenges.challenge: S6 is cited for the domestic price being set by a formula linked to the export reference price, but S6 describes only the export levy and reference price, not a domestic price formula.
challenges.answer: Softened: section 2 no longer claims a published domestic price formula; it says the domestic price is negotiated against export parity, the reference price net of the duty and levy S6 sets, which is the mechanic S6 supports [S6].

missing_bull_case.note: The 35 pct PT REA Kaltim associate is added to the bridge at book Rp1,579bn with no house or market value, and wood plus renewables (26 pct of revenue) are carried at a blended 20 pct gross margin with no separate valuation although wood ran at 11.2 pct in FY2025 and is the export leg the DHE relaxation helps.

missing_bear_case.note: The levy-plus-freight wedge is held flat at about USD281/t through 2030 and the bear carries only a -7 pct realisation shock; a progressive levy, or a DSI fair-price range that lifts the reference price and with it the levy base, is not scenarioed despite 88 pct palm exposure. The MSCI/liquidity de-rating is also absent from the bear.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E volume of 615 kt sits below the company's own +1 pct plan (~637 kt, S4 p.129) and other_revenue is held at zero volume growth; the realisation and FX basis itself is now honestly derived from 9M segment revenue and is consistent with low-end peers (LSIP 0.758, TLDN 0.750).

evidence_and_citations.note: Two related-party percentages are overstated 100x (0.68 pct read as 68.0 pct; 0.30 pct read as 30.0 pct), the 9M profit line F32 is mislabelled np_parent, the reverse-DCF implied price is 1,044 in s4 but 1,068 in the QC justification, and S6 is cited for a domestic price formula it does not state.

valuation_method_fit.note: The DCF carries 60 pct weight and implies EV/EBITDA of 8.3x FY2026E (32,957/3,982) against the analyst's own 6.34x method and the market's 4.05x; s4 explains the P/BV gap but not the EV/EBITDA gap, and the through-cycle CPO price is not anchored to a named 10y real average or cost-curve incentive price.

bias_and_tone.note: s4 says the market is assuming the price stays roughly where it is now, but its own reverse DCF is USD1,044 versus spot USD1,180; the report is also 7,194 words against a 3,500 guide, after the prior round had already cut it to 5,633.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Realisation 0.757 and terminal growth 2.5 pct sit inside the peer band (LSIP and TLDN at 0.750 to 0.758; many peers at 2.5 pct), but the DCF-implied multiple is far above what peers trade on today (AALI 3.0x; DSNG market 4.05x FY2026E).

conservatism_audit.note: Volume is 3.5 pct below the company plan and other_revenue has zero volume growth, both without a source; by contrast capex at 88 pct of D&A and the 2.5 pct escalator are now justified, and the realisation is derived rather than fitted to EBITDA.

calibration.note: All three BLOCK flags are cleared with sourced justifications; the -19 pct calibration gap is a price/FX artifact that reproduces FY2025 operating EBITDA of 3,814.6 at FY2025's own realisation 0.874 and rate 16,448, not a cost-structure break.

signoff.notes: Engine BUY tp 2,800 TR 115.2% reconciles: base 2,825, bear 806, bull 4,746 at 50/25/25 weight to 2,800; DCF 3,077 (60%), EV/EBITDA 2,165 at 6.3x FY2025A operating EBITDA 3,814.6 and P/BV 1,181 at 1.3x pre-revaluation book. The -61.6% P/BV warning is resolved in section 4: the leg uses attributable equity less the Rp2,585.1bn land revaluation surplus [F62, F63], which is what the earnings-quality card requires, and it is labelled a floor rather than a fair-value cross-check. 2 FIX and 5 NOTE items all answered; 3,500 words sits exactly at the update guide. The FY2025 capex restatement to Rp856.267bn (0.48x pack) is sourced to the Rp1,019.857bn plasma collection in the same investing section [F11], and the calibration gap is reproduced at FY2025 own realisation and FX. Peer-relative check: the target is not the peer case - DSNG carries its own 0.757 realisation and Rp8.02m/t cost against AALI 0.779/12.97m and LSIP 0.758/7.99m. Same liquidity-discount note as AALI.

bias.note: Base follows the company's own +1% volume plan (637 kt, F60/F23) and the house CPO deck; FY2026E realisation 0.757 is below FY2025A 0.874 and the FY2026E deck of USD1,135 is below spot USD1,180, so the base is not optimistic on price. No unsourced drift on volume, cost or royalty (royalty 0.0 is sourced: the palm line is all domestic, F61; the levy reaches it through parity). Scenarios mirror the same four drivers (CPO x0.8/x1.2, volume x0.95/x1.05, FX x0.9/x1.1, realisation x0.9/x1.1) with base 50%, bear 25%, bull 25%.

findings.finding: s4 says each extra turn on 'the annualised nine-month profit' adds 'a little over a per cent of enterprise value' and quotes IDR144.4bn. IDR144.4bn is the nine-month share (F70), not annualised (~IDR192.6bn), and 144.4/33,838 EV = 0.43% (0.57% annualised), not >1%.
findings.answer: Corrected: the associate is now marked at 8.2x the annualised nine-month share, a third again the 144.430 booked in the nine months, and the extra turn is stated as about half a per cent of the 33,838 enterprise value, not over one per cent [S2, F70].

findings.finding: s5 says the bear trims 'volume and the rupiah a twentieth each', but the m.usd_idr shock is 0.90 (a tenth); only volume is 0.95 (a twentieth). The assumptions narrative correctly says 'the rupiah strengthens a tenth'.
findings.answer: The bear sentence now says the rupiah strengthens a tenth, matching the 0.90 m.usd_idr shock; only volume is a twentieth, as the assumptions narrative has it [S3, S6].

findings.finding: s3 and s6 say 'no material pledge disclosed', but S2 notes show bearer plants Rp2,605.8bn, inventories Rp227.6bn and trade receivables Rp135.5bn pledged as collateral for BCA bank loans.
findings.answer: Wording changed to no share pledge in sections one and six, and the secured assets are stated with figures: bearer plants 2,605.8, inventories 227.6 and receivables 135.5 pledged for the BCA loans, all new facts [S2, F82, F83, F84].

findings.finding: s3 asserts a standard main-board listing with no special notation without a source; the earnings-quality card item 3 requires a sourced IDX board/notation status.
findings.answer: The unsourced main-board claim is removed. Section three now says the 2013 listing is sourced [S4] but the exchange board and notation status is not in the archived record, since idx.co.id is refused by design, so no status is asserted [S3, S4].

findings.finding: The VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL output contract requires a cost-curve quartile and reserve life; the report gives unit cash cost and planted area but no global cash-cost quartile.
findings.answer: Asset life and cost position added: mature plantations are amortised over a 20-year productive life, new fact F85, and 111,900 hectares imply about 4,500 ha of replanting a year; the unit cash cost is shown in USD per tonne against the 886 World Bank trough and the 978.9 reference price, with an explicit statement that no published global cost curve covers DSNG so no quartile is claimed [S3, S16, F85, F79, F48].

findings.finding: 4,396 words against the 500-3,500 update guide (lint warning); still 26% over after last round's cut.
findings.answer: Cut from 4,396 to 3,498 words, inside the 500-3,500 update guide and now lint PASS with no word warning: the DSI repetition and the previous-version changelog sentences are gone, the signpost paragraph is merged into the liquidity one, and no sourced figure was dropped.

findings.finding: s4/thesis say the DCF EV 'lands on the 6.3x of the cross-check' on FY2027E EBITDA; 33,838/5,435 = 6.23x, i.e. 6.2x, marginally below the 6.34x cross-check multiple.
findings.answer: Section four and the first thesis bullet now say the DCF EV is a little below the 6.3x cross-check on FY2027E EBITDA, 33,838 over 5,435 equals 6.23x, instead of landing on it [S3, S4].

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 3,064.3 vs the actual 3,814.6 (-20%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The gate re-prices FY2025 at the FY2026E realisation of 0.757 and the FY2026E rupiah of 17,570, both of which post-date the actual year: the realised rupiah price rose only 3% between the two periods while the dollar benchmark rose 12.7% [F3, S2], so the re-price understates FY2025 revenue. At FY2025's own realisation of 0.874 and rate of 16,448 the identical cost, D&A and opex structure reproduces FY2025 operating EBITDA of Rp3,814.6bn — operating profit plus D&A, the associate excluded and no impairment add-back, the definition section 3 of the report sets out and reconciles to the audited note-43 Rp4,078.0bn [F64, F65, F66, F67] — so there is no cost-structure break [F5, F9].

flags.message: capex FY2025A restated at 0.48x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's Rp1,799.927bn is the sum of fixed-asset additions 648.177, capitalised plantation cost 208.090 and the plasma-plantation outlay 943.660, but it ignores the Rp1,019.857bn of plasma collections in the same investing section, which reimburses that outlay [F11]. Own capex is therefore Rp856.267bn, 0.48x the pack; the plasma programme is a pass-through receivable, not a net use of cash.

flags.message: expected return +115%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers on one enterprise-value base. First the cycle: the deck's FY2027E CPO of USD1,240/t rests on the GAPKI 2.2m-tonne 2027 output decline [F37, S8], and the reverse DCF says today's price discounts USD1,040/t, 16% below that deck and 12% below the USD1,180 spot [S0]. Second the multiple: the DCF EV of Rp33,838bn is 8.3x the FY2026E operating EBITDA of Rp4,095bn but 6.2x FY2027E and 6.8x FY2030E, with an implied exit of 6.9x on FY2035 EBITDA of Rp5,948bn, so the DCF capitalises at the same 6.34x the EV/EBITDA cross-check applies; the market's 4.1x is the outlier, not the DCF [S3, S4]. Third the balance sheet: the Rp1,579bn associate at book, 9.4x last year's share of its profit, and net debt at half a year of EBITDA against a Rp14,045bn market capitalisation [F44, F52, F43]. The target is the weighted arithmetic of a 0.6-weight DCF at an 11.25% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth; the risk that the discount persists is section 5, not a modelling error.

news.title: Eddy Martono: El Niño Ancam Produksi Sawit 3 Juta Ton, GAPKI Minta Pemerintah Jaga Stabilitas Kebijakan
news.note: GAPKI chairman Eddy Martono said El Nino drought and fires could cut Indonesian palm output by up to 3 million tonnes and asked government to keep policy stable.

news.title: IPOC 2026: Ekspor Sawit Indonesia Tembus US$28,84 Miliar hingga Oktober 2026, Naik 60%
news.note: GAPKI conference data showed Indonesian palm exports reached US$28.84bn for January-October 2026, up 60% year on year.

news.title: GAPKI Peringatkan Ancaman Produktivitas Sawit, Pemupukan dan Replanting Jadi Tantangan Besar
news.note: GAPKI warned that Indonesian palm output growth faces structural constraints from limited fertiliser use and slow replanting by smallholders, speaking at its Nusa Dua conference.

news.title: Hadapi Risiko Ekspor Turun ke 26,5 Juta Ton akibat B50, GAPKI Desak Skema Fair Burden Sharing dan Akselerasi PSR
news.note: Gapki proposed flexible biodiesel blending, warning 2027 palm-oil exports could fall to about 26.5 million tonnes under full B50 plus El Nino, and urged fair burden sharing and faster PSR.

news.title: GAPKI Minta Peran DSI Dibatasi Sebagai Perantara, Bukan Eksportir Tunggal
news.note: GAPKI asked the government to limit PT DSI's role to intermediary, not sole exporter, citing export competitiveness and smooth palm exports.

news.title: Ekspor Batu Bara-CPO Lewat DSI Resmi 1 Januari 2027, Ini Caranya
news.note: Coal, CPO and ferro alloy exports through PT DSI become effective 1 January 2027, per the newly reported export mechanism.

news.title: Kadin dan GAPKI Sambut Relaksasi Konversi DHE SDA hingga 100%
news.note: Kadin and GAPKI welcome a government plan to allow up to 100% conversion of natural-resource export proceeds (DHE SDA) into rupiah, which they say eases exporter cash flow. Plan not yet implemented.

news.title: 4 catatan Gapki kala ekspor sawit cs satu pintu lewat Danantara
news.note: Gapki set out four notes on routing palm oil exports through Danantara, asking government to ensure PT DSI's intermediary fee does not burden exporters or hurt domestic CPO prices and farmers.

news.title: 4 catatan Gapki kala ekspor sawit cs satu pintu lewat Danantara
news.note: GAPKI asked government to ensure PT DSI's fee as sole palm-oil export intermediary via Danantara does not burden exporters or hurt domestic CPO prices and farmers.

news.title: Beban Ekspor CPO Turun 20 Persen di November, Manfaat bagi Rupiah Bergantung pada B50
news.note: Total CPO export levy and duty fell 20% in November to USD 246.36 per tonne from USD 308.27 in October.

news.title: El Nino Menekan Ekspor Minyak Sawit Indonesia
news.note: Kontan report: El Nino seen cutting Indonesia palm oil production by about 2.2 million tonnes next year versus this year, weighing on exports.
